guides.title: New Year's Eve on Cape Cod 2026: Fireworks, First Night and First Day Events
keywords: things to do in cape cod new years eve
cape cod new years eve events
provincetown new years eve drone show

facts.q: What is there to do on Cape Cod on New Year's Eve 2026?
facts.a: The two biggest public celebrations we found are First Night Chatham, its 36th New Year's Eve celebration, running from the noon Town Photo at Chatham Lighthouse until 10 PM, and Provincetown's First Light drone show over Provincetown Harbor at about 6 PM. Several libraries hold Noon Year's Eve countdowns for kids and families, and the Cotuit Center for the Arts has comedy shows at 5, 7 and 9 PM.

facts.q: Are there New Year's Eve fireworks on Cape Cod in 2026?
facts.a: Yes, in Chatham. First Night Chatham's fireworks follow the Noise Parade at 6:30 PM at Oyster Pond, a new location this year, and they're button-free. Provincetown's New Year's Eve show is a 300-drone display over the harbor at about 6 PM.

facts.q: When is the Provincetown New Year's Eve drone show?
facts.a: Thursday, December 31, 2026, beginning at approximately 6 PM over Provincetown Harbor. The MacMillan Pier lot and the areas around it are the main public viewing area, with free parking there and throughout town.

facts.q: How much are First Night Chatham buttons?
facts.a: Adult buttons (17 and up) are $30, rising to $35 as of December 15; children's buttons (ages 3–16) are $5, and children 2 and under are free. All outdoor activities and some indoor ones are button-free.

facts.q: Is there a polar plunge on Cape Cod on New Year's Day 2027?
facts.a: Yes. Provincetown's 11th annual Polar Bear Plunge is at noon on Friday, January 1, 2027, from the 14 Johnson Street parking lot, with single registration at $65 ($71.40 including the online fee). Yarmouth's Polar Plunge is at noon the same day at Bass River Beach (Smugglers Beach) in South Yarmouth, benefiting the Yarmouth Senior Center.
sources: Friends of Yarmouth Council on Aging (FOYCOA), via Eventbrite

facts.q: Are there First Day hikes on Cape Cod on January 1, 2027?
facts.a: Yes. Barnstable Land Trust lists First Day Hikes Cape Cod on Friday, January 1, 2027, a one-day regional celebration of free walks, talks and hikes, though individual hikes weren't posted when we checked. The Chatham Conservation Foundation's free First Day Hike on the Barclay's Pond Trail runs from 10 to 11 AM, with registration required.

facts.q: Do Cape Cod buses run on New Year's Day?
facts.a: No. CCRTA's fall/winter 2026 riders guide says there is no service on Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.

guides.title: Cape Cod Holiday Events 2026: Strolls, Parades, Lights and Markets

facts.q: When is the Falmouth Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: The Falmouth Village Holiday Stroll is Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 4 to 8 PM on Main Street and Queen's Buy Way, with the lighting of the Village Green at 6 PM, according to the Falmouth Chamber of Commerce's tentative 2026 schedule, which it says is subject to change.

facts.q: When is the Falmouth Christmas parade in 2026?
facts.a: Sunday, December 6, 2026, at noon, rain or shine, according to the Falmouth Chamber of Commerce's 2026 parade packet, which has the 63rd annual parade staging on Dillingham Avenue. The chamber's tentative schedule has it heading along Main Street to the Village Green.

facts.q: When is the Chatham Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Chatham's Christmas by the Sea weekend is Friday through Sunday, December 11–13, 2026, according to the Chatham Chamber of Commerce. The Christmas Stroll with the Merchants on Main runs Friday, December 11, from 4 to 9 PM, with a Light Parade with Santa at about 5:30 PM and the tree lighting at Sears Park at about 5:45 PM.

facts.q: When is the Hyannis Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: The organizers' Hyannis Holiday website lists the Main Street Stroll on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 11 AM to 3 PM on the Hyannis Village Green, and the Harbor Boat Parade from 4 to 6 PM at Hyannis Harbor, with the parade starting at 4:45 PM. The holiday weekend starts with a Sip & Shop on Friday, December 4, from 5 to 8 PM.
sources: Hyannis Holiday organizers (Arts Barnstable, Greater Hyannis Civic Association, Hyannis Main Street BID, Love Live Local and partners)
Hyannis Main Street Business Improvement District

facts.q: When is the Mashpee Christmas parade in 2026?
facts.a: Saturday, December 12, 2026. Mashpee Commons lists the Mashpee Holiday Stroll followed by the Mashpee Chamber Parade that day from 1 to 7:30 PM at Central Square, 22 Steeple Street.

facts.q: When is the Sandwich Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Sunday, December 13, 2026, from 11 AM to 4 PM. The Sandwich Chamber of Commerce is expanding its annual Village Stroll into a town-wide event this year.

facts.q: When is the Harwich Port Christmas stroll in 2026?
facts.a: Friday, December 4, 2026. The Harwich Chamber of Commerce's schedule starts the Harwich Port Stroll at 5:30 PM, the same time as the tree lighting and caroling in Doane Park, and Santa arrives by fire truck at 6:15 PM.

facts.q: When is Holly Folly 2026 in Provincetown?
facts.a: Holly Folly runs all four weekends in December 2026: December 4–6, 11–13, 18–20 and 25–27, according to the Provincetown Business Guild.

facts.q: When is the Pilgrim Monument lighting in 2026?
facts.a: Wednesday, November 25, 2026, Thanksgiving Eve. The Pilgrim Monument and Provincetown Museum's Annual Lighting On The Hill runs from 4 to 5:30 PM, the monument is lit at 5 PM, and the event is free.

facts.q: When does Gardens Aglow 2026 start?
facts.a: Gardens Aglow 2026 at Heritage Museums & Gardens in Sandwich opens November 27 and runs on select nights through December 27, from 4:30 to 8:30 PM with last entry at 8 PM.

facts.q: Is the Polar Express train running on Cape Cod in 2026?
facts.a: Yes. When we checked on November 8, 2026, Cape Cod Central Railroad's Polar Express page said "Tickets for 2026 now available!" The train departs from 70 Main Street in Buzzards Bay, and the ticket page lists an opening-weekend fare valid 11/20–11/22.

guides.title: Provincetown in the Off-Season: What's Open and What to Do

facts.q: Does the Provincetown ferry run in winter?
facts.a: No. Bay State Cruise Company's 2026 Boston–Provincetown season has concluded, and it says its 2027 season begins May 17. Capt. John Boats' Plymouth–Provincetown fast ferry is closed for the season. The Provincetown Business Guild lists Boston Harbor City Cruises as closed for the season, resuming May 15, 2027.

facts.q: How do you get to Provincetown in winter without a car?
facts.a: Cape Air flies four round trips a week between Boston and Provincetown from November 4, 2026, through May 12, 2027, at $109 one-way including taxes and fees. On the Cape, CCRTA's FLEX bus serves Harwich to Provincetown Monday through Saturday on its September 8, 2026–January 22, 2027 schedule, and rides on CCRTA fixed routes are free.

facts.q: What restaurants are open in Provincetown in winter?
facts.a: The Provincetown Business Guild keeps a What's Open list, last updated November 19, 2026. It lists Bay Cafe as open 365 days a year, and Kohi Coffee, Liz's Cafe/Anybody's Bar and Mac's Fish House as open daily, while the Lobster Pot and Pepe's Wharf are closed for the season. The guild recommends reconfirming hours on each business's website or social media.

facts.q: Is the Pilgrim Monument open in winter?
facts.a: Only into early December. The Pilgrim Monument and Provincetown Museum is open Friday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and closed for the season starting December 6.

facts.q: Do you have to pay for parking in Provincetown in winter?
facts.a: The town's parking page says the paid parking season ends Monday, November 2, 2026, and resumes May 1, 2027; during the paid season, the MacMillan Pier lot is $4 an hour and the Grace Hall lot $3 an hour. The town's pages don't spell out off-season charges, so check the signs at the lot. On New Year's Eve, the town says free parking will be available at the MacMillan Pier lot and throughout town. Under town regulations, posted Emergency Snow Routes are tow-away zones with no parking in the event of snowfall.

facts.q: What is there to do in Provincetown on New Year's Eve?
facts.a: The town's First Light drone show is Thursday, December 31, 2026, at approximately 6 p.m. over Provincetown Harbor, with the MacMillan Pier lot as the main viewing area and free parking there and throughout town. The First Light celebration runs December 31, 2026, to January 3, 2027, and the Provincetown Polar Bear Plunge is Friday, January 1, 2027.
sources: Provincetown Polar Bear Plunge, via RunSignup

facts.q: Are Cape Cod National Seashore beaches open in Provincetown in winter?
facts.a: Yes. Race Point Beach is open, though its vault toilets and showers are closed, and Herring Cove Beach is open with year-round vault toilets in the parking lot. Beach entrance fee collection has ended for the season.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

guides.title: The Best Time to Visit Cape Cod, Month by Month

facts.q: What is the warmest month on Cape Cod?
facts.a: July. NOAA's 1991–2020 normals for Hyannis give July an average high of 80.8°F, just ahead of August at 79.7°F.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

facts.q: When is the ocean warmest on Cape Cod?
facts.a: August. NOAA's Coastal Water Temperature Guide lists average August water temperatures of 72.6°F at Woods Hole and 68.8°F at Chatham's Lydia Cove, the highest months at both stations. NOAA retired that guide in May 2025, though the data are still available.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

facts.q: What is the busiest month on Cape Cod?
facts.a: At Cape Cod National Seashore, August was the busiest month in 2025, with 672,062 recreation visits. The Park Service says the most popular months to visit the Seashore are June through September.
sources: National Park Service (IRMA visitor use statistics)
National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: When are lifeguards on duty at Cape Cod beaches?
facts.a: At the six Cape Cod National Seashore beaches, lifeguards are typically on duty from late June through Labor Day.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: When is whale watching season on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Dolphin Fleet in Provincetown runs from April to October and plans to reopen in April 2027. Separately, North Atlantic right whales typically arrive in Cape Cod Bay in early winter, with many staying through mid-May, according to the Center for Coastal Studies.

facts.q: Is September a good time to visit Cape Cod?
facts.a: It depends on what you want. September's average high at Hyannis is 73.1°F, and the water at Woods Hole averages 69.4°F. The Seashore recorded 452,870 recreation visits in September 2025, fewer than July's 548,533 and August's 672,062. Seashore lifeguards typically finish at Labor Day.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
National Park Service (IRMA visitor use statistics)
National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

guides.title: Is Cape Cod Worth Visiting? An Honest, Season-by-Season Answer
keywords: is cape cod busy in september
is cape cod worth visiting in the off season

facts.q: Is Cape Cod an island?
facts.a: No. The National Park Service describes Cape Cod as a large peninsula extending 60 miles into the Atlantic from the coast of Massachusetts. It is separated from the mainland by the Cape Cod Canal, a 17.4-mile sea-level waterway connecting Buzzards Bay and Cape Cod Bay, and the Sagamore and Bourne bridges over the canal are the only roadway connections between the Cape and the mainland.

facts.q: What is the busiest time of year on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Summer. MassDOT says traffic and congestion near the Cape Cod Canal are typically highest in summer, and the National Park Service says the most popular months to visit Cape Cod National Seashore are June through September. In 2025, August was the Seashore's busiest month, with 672,062 recreation visits.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: Is Cape Cod busy in September?
facts.a: Busier than spring or late fall, but less than midsummer. Cape Cod National Seashore recorded 452,870 recreation visits in September 2025, compared with 672,062 in August and 463,276 in June. The Park Service counts June through September as its most popular months. National Seashore lifeguards are typically on duty only through Labor Day.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: Is Cape Cod worth visiting in the off-season?
facts.a: The Seashore stays open year-round, though some visitor facilities close from November through April. Salt Pond Visitor Center in Eastham is the park's year-round visitor center, and the Seashore still recorded 115,743 recreation visits in January 2025. Seashore beach entrance fees are collected only in spring, summer and fall.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: Is Cape Cod expensive to visit?
facts.a: We haven't found an official source that puts a figure on the overall cost of a Cape Cod trip, so we list published fees instead. A standard Cape Cod National Seashore beach pass is $25 per private vehicle, $15 per person on foot or bicycle, or $60 for an annual pass, valid for the current season. Eastham's town daily beach parking pass was $30 per vehicle in 2026.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: How many people visit Cape Cod National Seashore?
facts.a: The National Park Service's visitor use statistics record 3,682,771 recreation visits to Cape Cod National Seashore in 2025. These count visits, not individual people, and only the Seashore, not the whole Cape. For 2024, the Park Service reported 3.8 million visitors.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

guides.title: Things to Do on Cape Cod in Winter: What's Open, Owl Walks, Skating and Concerts
keywords: things to do in cape cod in winter
cape cod winter activities for kids
cape cod winter getaways for couples

facts.q: Is Cape Cod National Seashore open in winter?
facts.a: Yes. The Seashore is open year-round, though some visitor facilities close from November through April. Salt Pond Visitor Center in Eastham is the year-round visitor center, and the Park Service says its 11 walking trails are open year-round. The Province Lands Visitor Center in Provincetown is open only from May through October.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: What museums are open on Cape Cod in winter?
facts.a: The Cape Cod Museum of Art in Dennis is open 52 weeks a year. From January 2027 through mid-April, the JFK Hyannis Museum is open Thursday through Saturday, 10 AM to 4 PM. PAAM in Provincetown is open Wednesday through Sunday, noon to 5 PM, and the Cape Cod Maritime Museum in Hyannis lists winter hours of Wednesday through Saturday, 10 AM to 4 PM. The Sandwich Glass Museum's galleries are open by appointment only in January, then Wednesday through Sunday from February 1 through late March.

facts.q: Is there public ice skating on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Yes. Falmouth Ice Arena holds public skating every Friday from 7:30 to 8:40 PM through June 25, 2027, for $8. Charles Moore Arena in Orleans has public skating Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM, plus Sundays (seasonally) from 1:30 to 3:30 PM, for $10, with $4 skate rentals.

facts.q: Is there a winter farmers market on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Yes. The Orleans Farmers' Market moves indoors every Saturday from December through April, 10 AM to noon, at 5 Namskaket Road in Orleans. It takes a break the week after Christmas.

facts.q: How cold is Cape Cod in winter?
facts.a: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals for Hyannis put the average January high at 39.9°F and low at 24.1°F, and the average February high at 41.0°F and low at 24.8°F.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

facts.q: Can you see seals and whales on Cape Cod in winter?
facts.a: Right whales typically arrive in Cape Cod Bay in early winter, and many stay through mid-May, according to the Center for Coastal Studies. Gray seal females at colonies such as Monomoy Island give birth from late December to mid-February.

guides.title: Cape Cod in November 2026: What's Open, What's On and What to Expect
keywords: things to do in cape cod in november

facts.q: What is the weather like on Cape Cod in November?
facts.a: NOAA's 1991–2020 climate normals for Hyannis (Barnstable Municipal Airport) give November an average high of 53.5°F, an average low of 37.3°F and 4.13 inches of precipitation.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

facts.q: What time does it get dark on Cape Cod in November?
facts.a: Early. Daylight saving time ended on November 1, 2026. The U.S. Naval Observatory's data for Hyannis puts sunset at 4:36 PM on November 1, 4:21 PM on November 15 and 4:12 PM on November 30, 2026.
sources: National Institute of Standards and Technology
U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department

facts.q: Are Cape Cod beaches open in November?
facts.a: Cape Cod National Seashore beaches such as Head of the Meadow and Herring Cove are listed as open, but beach entrance fee collection has ended for the season, and restrooms and showers are closed, though the vault toilets in those two beaches' parking lots are open year-round. Lifeguards are typically on duty at those beaches only from late June through Labor Day.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: Do the ferries to Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard run in November?
facts.a: Yes. The Steamship Authority runs daily, year-round service to both islands, and Hy-Line Cruises runs year-round Hyannis–Nantucket service. Hy-Line's Hyannis–Martha's Vineyard ferry has ended for the season.

facts.q: Can you go whale watching on Cape Cod in November?
facts.a: Hyannis Whale Watcher Cruises' last trip of 2026 was Sunday, November 1, and Captain John Boats in Plymouth is closed for the season. Last year, the first right whale of the 2025/26 season was reported from Race Point Beach by a member of the public on October 26, 2025.

facts.q: What is open on Cape Cod on Thanksgiving?
facts.a: It varies by business, so check ahead. In Provincetown, the chamber of commerce says most businesses are closed on Thursday, though some restaurants serve Thanksgiving menus, and shops, galleries and restaurants are open Friday through Sunday. The Cape Cod Museum of Natural History is closed on Thanksgiving Day.
sources: Cape Cod Museum of Natural History

guides.title: Cape Cod in December: Weather, Holiday Events and What's Open

facts.q: What is the weather like on Cape Cod in December?
facts.a: NOAA's 1991–2020 climate normals for Hyannis (Barnstable Municipal Airport) give December an average high of 45.2°F, an average low of 29.3°F, a mean temperature of 37.2°F and 4.68 inches of precipitation.
sources: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

facts.q: What time does it get dark on Cape Cod in December?
facts.a: Around 4:15 PM. U.S. Naval Observatory data for Hyannis puts sunset at 4:12 PM on December 1 and December 15, 4:14 PM on December 21 and 4:21 PM on December 31, 2026. The winter solstice is December 21, 2026, at 3:50 PM Eastern time.
sources: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department

facts.q: Are Cape Cod National Seashore beaches open in December?
facts.a: Yes. The Seashore is open year-round. As of November 17, 2026, the Park Service listed its beaches as open, with restrooms and showers closed and beach entrance fee collection ended for the season; vault toilets in the Head of the Meadow and Herring Cove parking lots are open year-round. Salt Pond Visitor Center in Eastham  was listed as open from 9 AM to 4:30 PM.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: Do the ferries to Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard run in December?
facts.a: The Steamship Authority runs daily, year-round service to both islands, and Hy-Line Cruises runs year-round Hyannis–Nantucket service. Hy-Line's Hyannis–Martha's Vineyard ferry has ended for the season.

facts.q: Do CCRTA buses run on Christmas Day?
facts.a: CCRTA's FLEX, H2O and Sealine routes don't run on Christmas Day or New Year's Day.

facts.q: Can you see whales on Cape Cod in December?
facts.a: Possibly. Right whales were detected in Cape Cod Bay in mid-November: NOAA Fisheries set a voluntary right whale Slow Zone there effective November 14–29, 2026. Slow Zones are based on sightings or acoustic detections of right whales and last 15 days, so check NOAA's current list.

guides.title: Sagamore and Bourne Bridge Traffic: Peak Times and When to Cross
keywords: best time to cross sagamore bridge
best time to travel to cape cod on saturday

facts.q: When is Sagamore Bridge traffic the worst?
facts.a: MassDOT's traffic studies say traffic volumes and congestion near the Cape Cod Canal are typically highest in the summer, and its bridge project's traffic report identifies the summer Saturday midday as the peak period for total canal crossings in both directions. Summer Saturdays are busy because vacation rentals on the Cape generally begin and end on Saturday.

facts.q: What is the best time to cross the Cape Cod bridges?
facts.a: None of the MassDOT studies or advisories we reviewed names a single best time to cross. MassDOT's 2014 counts show both bridges carry far less traffic outside summer: in an October 2014 count, about 41,400 vehicles a day on the Sagamore and 38,000 on the Bourne, versus 65,900 and 56,500 in August. MassDOT also says that 85% of the year, traffic is at or below the level of the fall weekday afternoon peak period. Check live conditions before you leave.

facts.q: How many cars cross the Sagamore Bridge each day?
facts.a: In 2019 the Sagamore Bridge averaged 61,990 vehicles a day and the Bourne Bridge 46,500, according to MassDOT's Cape Cod Bridges environmental impact statement.

facts.q: Who owns the Sagamore and Bourne bridges?
facts.a: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers owns, operates and maintains both bridges. MassDOT is leading the project to replace them, starting with the Sagamore Bridge.
sources: Office of Governor Maura Healey / MassDOT (Mass.gov)

facts.q: Will the Sagamore Bridge close during the replacement?
facts.a: MassDOT says it plans to maintain two lanes of traffic in each direction throughout construction, and its hearing FAQ says at least two travel lanes will stay open in each direction across the canal.
sources: Office of Governor Maura Healey / MassDOT (Mass.gov)

facts.q: When does construction on the new Sagamore Bridge start?
facts.a: MassDOT's September 28, 2026, release says a Notice to Proceed is anticipated in late 2027, with construction expected to begin in winter 2027; its public hearing FAQ says major construction is expected to begin in spring 2028. MassDOT expects the new eastbound span to open in 2033.
sources: Office of Governor Maura Healey / MassDOT (Mass.gov)

facts.q: How do I check Cape Cod bridge traffic right now?
facts.a: MassDOT's Mass511 website and app show live cameras, travel times and real-time traffic conditions, and you can dial 511 and select a route to hear real-time conditions. The Cape Cod Commission also points to MassDOT's GoTime app and the Army Corps' Cape Cod Canal bridge alerts.

guides.title: Whales and Seals on Cape Cod in Winter: Where to Look and How Close You Can Get
keywords: where to see seals on cape cod
best time to see whales off cape cod

facts.q: When is the best time to see right whales on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Right whales typically arrive in Cape Cod Bay in early winter, and many stay through mid-May. April is typically the peak of the season, though in 2025/26 March was the busiest month in Cape Cod Bay.

facts.q: Can you see right whales from shore on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Yes, especially in spring. Right whales often feed very close to shore, offering watchers on the beach unbeatable views, according to the Center for Coastal Studies, and the National Park Service says whales can often be seen from shore at Provincetown's Race Point Beach in spring.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore

facts.q: How close can you get to a right whale?
facts.a: Federal regulations prohibit approaching or remaining within 500 yards (1,500 feet) of a right whale, whether by boat, by aircraft including drones, or on a surfboard, kayak or jet ski, and the Center for Coastal Studies notes the limit applies to paddle-boarders and swimmers too. Massachusetts regulations also bar any vessel in state waters, or registered in Massachusetts, from entering the 500-yard zone around a surfacing right whale. You can still watch from the beach: right whales often feed very close to shore.

facts.q: Where can you see seals on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Monomoy National Wildlife Refuge off Chatham: South Monomoy Island contains the largest gray seal haul-out site on the U.S. Atlantic coast. On the refuge's mainland trails at Morris Island in Chatham, the refuge says you may see "the occasional seal".

facts.q: How far should you stay from seals?
facts.a: NOAA's viewing guideline is at least 150 feet (50 yards), and to limit your viewing to 30 minutes or less. Federal law prohibits harming or harassing them, and feeding them is against the law. Touching or trying to touch a seal violates the Marine Mammal Protection Act.
sources: NOAA Fisheries, Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office

facts.q: Who do I call about a stranded seal or whale on Cape Cod?
facts.a: Call the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) at (508) 743-9548, which covers Cape Cod and southeastern Massachusetts, or NOAA's Northeast Marine Mammal and Sea Turtle Stranding and Entanglement Hotline at (866) 755-6622.

facts.q: What should I do if I find a sea turtle on a Cape Cod beach in winter?
facts.a: Don't put it back in the water, and don't assume it's dead: turtles that look lifeless are often still alive. Mass Audubon asks you to move it above the high tide line without grabbing it by the head or flippers, cover it completely with seaweed (never sand), mark the spot, and call its Wellfleet Bay hotline at 508-349-2615, option 2.
sources: Mass Audubon, Wellfleet Bay Wildlife Sanctuary
